steps.say: Stromal tumours of the small bowel are judged by size and division rate. Big or busy ones need years of tablets after removal, while small quiet ones are cured by a limited bowel resection.
steps.tx: Small bowel **GIST** (gut pacemaker tumour) over **5 cm** (five centimetres) or over 5 mitoses per 5 square mm is high risk per **modified NIH** (risk scoring) criteria, needing **3 years** (three years) of adjuvant imatinib after R0 segmental resection with clear margins and long follow-up.

vis.alt: Multinodular stomach tumour with nodal spread and microscopic views of tumour cells and markers.
vis.caption: Gastric GIST: multinodular tumour with nodal spread, epithelioid cells and KIT staining. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: Tumours in tight corners shrink with tablets first so the surgeon can save the organ. Scans track the melting by density change, and the operation follows once the lump is small enough.
steps.tx: **Neoadjuvant imatinib** (pre-surgery tablets) for **6 to 12 months** (six to twelve months) shrinks borderline duodenal and rectal GIST for organ-preserving surgery, with response judged by **Choi criteria** (scan density rules) on contrast imaging over the treatment months until surgery.

steps.say: Hormone tumours of the small bowel tether the mesentery into a hard mass and flush the face with diarrhoea. The involved loop comes out with its glands, and monthly injections control the hormones.
steps.tx: Small bowel neuroendocrine tumours with mesenteric **desmoplastic** (scarring) mass and flushing-diarrhoea **carcinoid syndrome** (hormone storm) need bowel resection with mesenteric nodal clearance plus **octreotide** (hormone-calming injections) for lasting control of flushing and diarrhoea every single day long term together always.

steps.say: Giant fatty tumours behind the belly lining are removed with everything they touch, since shelling them out guarantees return. The well-behaved kind recurs locally while the aggressive kind spreads far.
steps.tx: **Retroperitoneal sarcoma** (behind-lining cancer) over **10 cm** (ten centimetres) needs **compartmental resection** (whole-zone removal) with adjacent organs at specialist centres, with well-differentiated **liposarcoma** (fat cancer) recurring locally in the same bed repeatedly despite apparent complete removal at expert surgery last year.

steps.say: The gristly scar-like lumps after surgery or in polyposis families often melt away alone and return if cut. Drugs that choke their blood supply work better than the knife for growing ones.
steps.tx: **Desmoid fibromatosis** (aggressive scar tumour) in FAP or after surgery is watched first with **20 percent** (twenty percent) spontaneous regression, and **sorafenib** (blood-starving tablet) or low-dose chemotherapy suits progressive disease over surgery with fewer late harmful effects on the young growing patient cohort today.

steps.say: A precancerous growth on the bile drainage nipple is removed through the opened duodenum when small, but bigger or deeper ones need the full Whipple operation because cancer hides inside.
steps.tx: Duodenal adenoma with high-grade dysplasia or **ampullary adenoma** (nipple growth) over **3 cm** (three centimetres) needs transduodenal **ampullectomy** (nipple removal) or Whipple for invasive cancer risk in the complex ampullary region of the duodenum near bile entry always here clinically.

steps.say: Hamartoma polyps in the inherited spots-and-freckles syndrome drag the bowel into itself and block it. Big ones are fished out with the scope, and heavy burdens are cleared in one open sitting.
steps.tx: **Peutz-Jeghers** (spots-freckles polyp syndrome) small bowel polyps over **1.5 cm** (one and a half centimetres) get **enteroscopic polypectomy** (scope removal) with **enteroscopy** (deep scope pass) to prevent **intussusception** (telescoped bowel), with clean sweep laparotomy and intraoperative scoping for heavy burden.

vis.alt: Telescoped bowel with trapped mesentery and a bullseye scan appearance.
vis.caption: Intussusception from polyp lead points: telescoped loop with target sign on ultrasound. Credit: StewardMD.

steps.say: True cancers of the small bowel are rare and show up late with blockage near the top. A wide removal with the draining glands plus drug treatment afterwards gives the best chance.
steps.tx: Primary **small bowel adenocarcinoma** (true bowel cancer) of the duodenum and **proximal jejunum** (upper small bowel) presents with obstruction and needs **segmental resection** (length removal) with nodal clearance and adjuvant chemotherapy for cure in suitable patients after full recovery from surgery.
